discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, founding moiré quantum matter

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional and moiré quantum materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that two graphene sheets twisted to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees have nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realized this with tear-and-stack fabrication and found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity, tuned by a gate in a single device. This established twist angle as a new control knob for quantum matter. Many groups worldwide have reproduced the results. The work founded the field of moiré quantum materials, which has since revealed orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, Wigner crystals, moiré excitons and, in twisted semiconductors and rhombohedral graphene, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states that support anyons at zero magnetic field. Few discoveries in condensed matter have opened so much new physics so quickly, and it is a model of theory and experiment working together.
